title: Spectral Survival Analysis

problem.claim: Scaling CoxPH to large datasets and deep architectures is challenging, particularly in high-dimensional settings.

gap.claim: Existing CoxPH methods and variants do not adequately address scalability for large, high-dimensional datasets and deep architectures.

contributions.claim: The paper connects rank regression with the CoxPH model and adapts a spectral method for rank regression to survival analysis.
The approach generalizes to several CoxPH variants, including deep models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method was empirically evaluated on multiple real-world high-dimensional datasets.
The authors report that their method outperforms legacy methods in predictive performance and efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Survival analysis is widely used across multiple fields.
CoxPH is a commonly encountered semi-parametric survival model.
Scaling CoxPH to large datasets and deep architectures is difficult in high-dimensional regimes.
The authors use a connection between rank regression and CoxPH to adapt a spectral method to survival analysis.
The approach covers multiple CoxPH variants, including deep models, and is evaluated on real-world high-dimensional datasets with reported gains over legacy methods.

source_observation.claim: A connection between rank regression and CoxPH enables adaptation of a spectral method to survival analysis.

interpretation.claim: Relating a target model to a better-understood problem can provide a route to scalable algorithm design.

application.claim: When improving survival models, investigate structural connections to regression formulations that already have scalable methods.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this transfer is applicable beyond the described CoxPH variants or survival-analysis setting.

source_observation.claim: The method is reported to scale across multiple real-world high-dimensional datasets and outperform legacy methods in predictive performance and efficiency.

interpretation.claim: Evaluating both predictive performance and computational efficiency is relevant when addressing scalability.

application.claim: Assess scalable methods using representative high-dimensional data and report both model quality and efficiency.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide dataset identities, baselines, metrics, or experimental conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the spectral algorithm, optimization procedure, or theoretical guarantees.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline configurations, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe computational resource requirements or reproducibility details.
